gdpr.note: Any organization determining or carrying out processing.

ccpa.note: Businesses that meet a threshold, plus some affiliates and joint ventures, which can include non-profits.

pipl.note: Any organization or individual determining processing.

ukgdpr.note: The same controller and processor model as the EU GDPR.

fadp.note: Private controllers and federal government bodies.

pdpa-ar.note: Any file, register, or databank holding personal data.

lpdp-uy.note: Data held by public and private entities.

pipa-kr.note: Any entity processing personal information for its work.

appi.note: Any business using a personal information database.

nzpa.note: A broad definition covering nearly all organizations.

popia.note: Public and private bodies, and individuals, that determine processing.

kdpa.note: Mirrors the GDPR controller and processor split.

dpdp.note: Any person determining the purpose and means of processing.

pipeda.note: Private-sector organizations handling personal information commercially, plus federally regulated employers for staff data.

pa-au.note: Commonwealth agencies and private businesses, with some exemptions.

pdpa-sg.note: Any organization handling personal data in Singapore, including non-profits.

gdpr.value: EU establishment, or people in the EU

ccpa.note: Regardless of where the business is located.

lgpd.value: Processing in or of people in Brazil

pipl.note: Extraterritorial for offering goods or profiling.

ukgdpr.value: UK establishment, or people in the UK
ukgdpr.note: An establishment counts wherever the processing happens. Foreign firms are covered when they target or monitor people in the UK.

fadp.note: Applies to conduct that produces effects in Switzerland.

pdpa-ar.note: Data held or processed within the country.

lpdp-uy.note: Includes foreign controllers that target or analyze people in Uruguay, or use means there.

pipa-kr.note: Reaches overseas handlers where Korean users are affected.

appi.value: Handling data of people in Japan
appi.note: Extraterritorial where goods or services target people in Japan.

nzpa.value: Agencies acting in or from NZ
nzpa.note: Includes overseas agencies carrying on business in New Zealand.

popia.note: Responsible party domiciled in, or using means in, the country.

kdpa.value: Processing in or of people in Kenya
kdpa.note: Controllers and processors established or acting in Kenya.

dpdp.value: Processing in India or targeting India
dpdp.note: Extraterritorial where linked to offering goods or services in India.

pipeda.value: Canada, except in-province activity under similar provincial laws
pipeda.note: Quebec, Alberta and British Columbia apply their own laws inside those provinces.

pa-au.value: Australia, plus overseas firms with an Australian link
pa-au.note: Covers overseas organizations that carry on business in Australia.

pdpa-sg.note: Covers personal data handled in Singapore, including data brought in from overseas.

gdpr.note: Applies to any size, though duties scale with risk.

ccpa.value: About $26.6M revenue, 100k consumers, or 50% data revenue
ccpa.note: Meet one or more to be covered. The revenue figure rises with inflation every two years.

pipl.note: But high volume triggers extra localization and assessment duties.

ukgdpr.note: Applies to any size. Duties scale with risk.

fadp.note: Businesses under 250 employees need no record of processing, unless their processing is high-risk.

appi.note: The small-business exemption was removed in 2017.

nzpa.note: Applies to agencies of any size.

kdpa.note: Registration depends on turnover, staff numbers and listed purposes.

dpdp.note: Applies regardless of size. The government can exempt notified fiduciaries, such as startups, from some duties.

pipeda.note: Applies to organizations of any size.

pa-au.note: Smaller businesses are exempt unless they handle health data, trade in data, or fit another exception.

pdpa-sg.note: No size, revenue or volume threshold.

ccpa.note: Government is excluded. Most non-profits are too, unless tied to a covered business.

pipl.note: State organs covered, with some exceptions.

fadp.note: Federal bodies. Cantonal bodies fall under cantonal law.

pipa-kr.note: Public institutions and private entities alike.

appi.note: Public bodies were brought under the APPI by the 2021 amendment.

dpdp.note: Applies to the State, subject to specific exemptions.

pipeda.note: Federal institutions fall under a separate Privacy Act. Provincial laws cover provincial bodies.

pa-au.note: Covers Commonwealth agencies. State agencies follow state rules, where they exist.

pdpa-sg.note: Public agencies are excluded and follow separate public-sector rules.

ccpa.note: Any qualifying business that does business in California and handles residents' data.

fadp.note: Effects-based reach. Foreign controllers may need a Swiss representative.

pdpa-ar.note: Chiefly territorial, with outward transfer controls.

lpdp-uy.note: Reaches foreign controllers offering goods or services to people in Uruguay, or analyzing their behavior.

pipa-kr.note: Reaches overseas handlers affecting Korean residents.

appi.note: Reaches foreign operators targeting people in Japan.

nzpa.note: Reaches overseas agencies carrying on business in New Zealand.

popia.note: Where means located in South Africa are used.

kdpa.note: Reaches controllers acting on people in Kenya.

dpdp.note: Reaches processing outside India linked to offering goods or services there.

pipeda.note: Courts apply it to foreign organizations with a real and substantial connection to Canada.

pa-au.note: Reaches overseas businesses operating in Australia, wherever the data is held.

pdpa-sg.note: Foreign organizations are covered when they handle personal data in Singapore.
